At about 14:08 local time (13:08 UTC) on 10 December 2005, Flight 1145 from Abuja crash-landed at Port Harcourt International Airport. The plane, a McDonnell Douglas DC-9-32 with 110 people on board slammed into the ground and burst into flames. Immediately after the crash, seven survivors were recovered and taken to hospitals, but it has since been reported that four of those survivors have died in hospital care, leaving three survivors, two of whom were flown to South Africa. In the end, two people survived. Conclusion Nigeria Accident Investigation Bureau finally concluded that the probable cause of the crash was due to the crew's decision to continue the approach beyond the Decision Altitude without having the runway insight.

In January 2009 Harold Demuren , the director general of the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA), said that the families of the air crash victims would be compensated and that Sosoliso had already paid $2.3 million into an escrow account to compensate the families.
At about 14:08 local time (13:08 UTC) on 10 December 2005, Flight 1145 from Abuja crash-landed at Port Harcourt International Airport.

Immediately after the crash, seven survivors were recovered and taken to hospitals, but it has since been reported that four of those survivors have died in hospital care, leaving three survivors, two of whom were flown to South Africa.
It entered the Nigerian registration on 12 June 2003.
Passengers and crews The captain was Benjamin Adekunle Adebayo, a 48 year old Nigerian with a total flying experience of 10.050 hours with 1.900 of them were on the DC-9.
All seven crew members and 101 of the 103 passengers died in the crash, or later from their injuries.
Among the passengers were about sixty-one secondary school students from Loyola Jesuit College in the Federal Capital Territory region of Nigeria.
Rising crime along roads during the 1990s made parents believe that road travel was too dangerous.

Weather analysis The Nigerian Accident Investigation Bureau found out that the data from satellite imagery by Boeing Aircraft Company in USA suggested that at 13:00 UTC, a sea breeze front, possibly reinforced by an outflow, pushed inland in the vicinity of Port Harcourt.
30 seconds before the crash, the aircraft descended for 7 seconds and leveled off at an altitude of 204 ft, which is below the Decision Altitude of 307 ft.
From the CVR data, 16 seconds before the crash, the Captain called for a go-around, gear up and flaps before the crash.
Eyewitness account Investigators conducted an interview with an eyewitness of the crash.
Firemen in the airport handling the crash were also stated bad weather condition were present, as they were forced to reposition their equipments due to high wind.
Legacy Andy and Ify Ilabor, the parents of crash victims Chuka, Nkem, and Busonma "Buso" Ilabor, started a foundation called the Ilabor Angels to assist orphans and AIDS victims.
The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) mandates that each family of an air crash victim is entitled to only 3 million naira or US$18,157 from the airline.
